results.question: How do I remove and reinstall the high-pressure seals on a 5CP6120?
results.answer:
⚠️ **Safety flag.** This task involves a hazard. Isolate and verify zero energy before hands-on work. (p.2)

Remove the manifold head, then with the crankcase side of the manifold facing up, use reverse pliers to remove the Lo-Pressure Seal from the Seal Case, remove the press-in style Seal Case from the Manifold Head, and remove the O-Ring from the outside diameter of the Seal Case; the 5CP6120 high-pressure seal is generally removable from the manifold without tools, unless it is extremely worn [1]. Reinstall the seal with the same type of seal and O-rings the pump was built with, and make sure the seal is fully seated before reassembly [1].

results.question: Can I crack the valve plugs open while the system is still pressurized to save time?
results.answer:
⚠️ **Safety flag.** This task involves a hazard. Isolate and verify zero energy before hands-on work. (p.1)

No — before servicing, shut off the drive and turn off the water supply to the pump, then relieve all discharge line pressure by triggering the gun or opening the discharge-line valve [2]. Opening the valve plugs under pressure is not supported in the service instructions and would risk injury and pump damage [2].
